verbalization: Caspofungin, an anti-infective agent, is implicated in reducing serum calcium levels, which is mediated by Gentamicin. Gentamicin binds to Slc22a6, a transporter protein involved in calcium homeostasis. This suggests a potential mechanism by which Caspofungin may influence Slc22a6 function, possibly through its interaction with Gentamicin. The observed relationship implies that Caspofungin could modulate the activity of Gentamicin, which in turn affects Slc22a6. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Caspofungin and Slc22a6, though the exact nature of this interaction remains to be elucidated. The pathway highlights the role of Gentamicin in mediating the effects of Caspofungin on calcium homeostasis, underscoring the importance of transporter proteins in drug action and physiological regulation.
